# ESP32-S3 refresh A/B at 80 MHz, both sessions on the board ending 3D:C8 (2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23): every image

rind's time for each image, in µs: the median over that image's flashes, with the number of flashes (n) and the spread (slowest − fastest flash) / fastest. A ratio is the image's median over the control's (`ctl`); below 1 is faster than the control. `ctl` was flashed 16 times; `zero` was flashed 2 times; `rot` was flashed 2 times; `notag` was flashed 2 times; `poly` was flashed 2 times; `all` was flashed 2 times; `xor` was flashed 2 times; `polyw` was flashed 2 times. An image flashed once has one run, so its spread is 0 and says nothing about repeatability; read it against the control's spread. The RustCrypto column is the median of every flash of every image (the same RustCrypto code in each image, a layout control). Every number here is recomputed from [ab-both-days.json](ab-both-days.json) by `cargo verify`.
Both sessions pooled, same board and same images: `d1-N` is flash N of the 2026-11-22 session ([its tree](../8a5977adb9c32ea2ed010c400f5ffbdcdec14b47-refresh-ab-80mhz-2026-11-22/NOTES.md)), `d2-N` flash N of the 2026-11-23 repeat (this tree). A flash is still one run; pooling gives each candidate two runs, which is one short of the three-run rule.
